title: Round 4 overview
read_this_first: Three columns side by side. Nothing is summed and there is no position: rows inside a tier are alphabetical.

judge_tier.label: Judge tier (Sonnet 5)
judge_tier.definition: Fixed letters on one judge's 1-5 `overall` mean (Sonnet 5, session_judge_v2.jsonl): A 3.8 and above, B 3.2-3.8, C 2.6-3.2, D 2.0-2.6, E below 2.0. Edges 5.0 - 0.6k, lower edge inclusive; A is open at the top and E at the floor. The letters are frozen and never re-lettered.
caveats: Two judge families. Sonnet 5 sets the letter; ChatGPT via Codex (subscription, blind) scored the same 1,328 sessions. Per model the two agree at Pearson r +0.87, and ChatGPT scores 0.94 lower on average (its scale offset). With the offset removed, 50 of 69 tiered models keep their letter and 19 change (`tier_depends_on_judge`). Neither judge is shown to be the right one (ROUND4_DESIGN 24; intervals in round4_second_judge.json).
Not the 'craft band' on the profile cards, which is the flaw hunter.
The interval covers which seeds were drawn, not judge disagreement.

J.label: J (round 4 judgment)
J.definition: Copied from round4_willingness_leaderboard.json, printed to 2 decimals. Treat models within ~0.3 as tied.

watch_out.label: Watch out
watch_out.definition: Counts, never a score. Scene-level items always show; turn-level items show at 2% of turns or more, and every count is in `counts`.

definitions.blank_scene: every model turn in the session has no visible text; the judge's score (1.0) stays in the mean
definitions.partial_scene: answered turns (at least 50 characters) under 70% of the seed's modal count (ROUND4_DESIGN 13a); kept as scored
definitions.stub_replies: a turn with fewer than 50 visible characters, including empty ones, outside blank scenes; denominator is every turn outside blank scenes
definitions.writes_your_character: production_defects.json selfplay rule: the reply writes a turn under the user character's speaker label; denominator is answered turns
definitions.leaks: production_defects.json leak rule: harness prompt, chat-template token or reasoning tag inside the reply
definitions.loops: production_defects.json loop rule: at least 35% of a turn's 8-grams repeat an earlier 8-gram in the same turn
definitions.defects_source: leak, writes-your-character and loop counts are recounted here with analyze_production_defects.py's own functions; for a model in production_defects.json the recount must equal the file, and a model the file skips (under 50 answered turns) is counted here
definitions.silent_refusal: round 4 Track A: at least 20% of replies empty and the empty rate at least 25 points higher on the most explicit rung than the mildest (analyze_round4_willingness.py rule); J cannot see it. The counts are recounted from the round 4 runs and must reproduce the published rate and slope
definitions.plays_itself: the model is also the user simulator for this corpus (config user_sim_model), so on its own row it talks to itself

judge_means.definition: Mean of the Sonnet 5 session judge's `overall` and of its S.5 agency, S.1 consistency and S.3 momentum session scores. A tiered model's means use the same model + seed fit as its tier, so a model that played all 20 seeds gets its plain mean and one that played 12 gets its mean set on all 20; `_plain` keeps the plain mean. An untiered model (under 12 seeds) gets plain means and no tier. Tiers are assigned on the unrounded `overall`.

chatgpt.name: chatgpt
chatgpt.label: ChatGPT via Codex (subscription, blind)
chatgpt.basis: the overview's own: the model + seed fit over the tiered pool with this judge's own seed effects (the plain mean for a model that played every seed); an untiered model gets its plain mean and no letter

scale_offset.method: mean over the 69 tiered models of Sonnet's model mean minus this judge's, each model weighted once; adding it gives both judges the same mean across these models

chatgpt.tier_rule: `tier`: this judge's mean on the same frozen letters (A 3.8 and above, B 3.2-3.8, C 2.6-3.2, D 2.0-2.6, E below 2.0), raw, so a judge that uses the scale lower reads lower letters for that reason alone
chatgpt.tier_depends_rule: `tier_depends_on_judge`: this judge's mean plus the scale offset falls in another letter than Sonnet's; the adjusted letter, with its interval, is in round4_second_judge.json
chatgpt.flag_rule: `flag`: |difference| > 0.3, the card's band; difference is this judge's mean plus the scale offset minus Sonnet's

self_preference.note: The sample all three families scored: 1 to 5 sessions per model, too few for a per-model figure. Nothing in the overview is adjusted by it. The tilt is relative: it cannot say whether Sonnet is generous to Claude or the others are harsh (ROUND4_DESIGN 17b). ChatGPT's figures on every session are in round4_second_judge.json (ROUND4_DESIGN 24).
self_preference.method: each judge rescaled to Sonnet's mean and sd over these sessions; tilt = mean(Sonnet - other) on Claude sessions minus the same on non-Claude sessions (vs_non_claude, the size a Claude-only correction uses) or on all sessions (vs_all_sessions); SE and 95% interval from 10000 draws that resample models with replacement, numpy default_rng(20260926), rescaling inside each draw

chatgpt.basis: Claude minus non-Claude (vs_non_claude): only Claude is shifted

gemini.basis: Claude minus non-Claude (vs_non_claude): only Claude is shifted

smallest_shift_that_moves_a_claude_model.note: a Claude-only shift has to exceed this to move any Claude model down a letter

human_multiturn_arena.note: Public file only. Spearman against the Sonnet 5 judge mean; p from 20000 label permutations.
